summary: Craig Cove Airport is a small domestic airfield on the western coast of Ambrym Island in Vanuatu, providing essential air access to one of the world's most volcanically active islands, home to the twin peaks of Mount Benbow and Mount Marum. The airport primarily serves local communities and adventure travelers drawn to Ambrym's dramatic volcanic landscapes and preserved Kastom (traditional) culture. Its remote location and short runway make it a gateway to one of the South Pacific's most geothermally dynamic destinations.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate flights to Craig Cove Airport?
A: Air Vanuatu provides scheduled domestic services connecting Craig Cove with Port Vila on Efate Island, typically using small turboprop aircraft suited to the short runway.

Q: How long is the flight from Port Vila to Craig Cove?
A: The flight takes approximately 45 minutes, covering the roughly 200 km across the Vanuatu archipelago.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: Craig Cove is a minimal airstrip with basic infrastructure, including a small terminal shelter; passengers should expect very limited amenities upon arrival.

Q: When is the best time to visit Ambrym Island?
A: The dry season from May to October offers the most reliable weather, clearer views of the volcanic craters, and safer trekking conditions.
transport_tips: Ground transport must be pre-arranged as there are no taxis
